key_insight: SpecGP is a transformer-based model that predicts energy-adaptable structural spectra for N-glycopeptides, increasing fragment ion coverage to improve isomer discrimination and boost identification confidence via rescoring.
problem_solved: Mass-spectrometry identification of glycopeptides is hampered by variable collision-energy-dependent fragmentation and sparse fragment coverage, making isomer discrimination and confident identifications difficult across instruments and conditions.
method: Transformer-based conditional model that takes glycopeptide sequence/structure and collision energy as inputs to predict structural fragment spectra.
Energy-adaptable prediction across diverse collision energies to capture shifting fragmentation patterns and improve fragment ion coverage.
Use predicted spectra to rescore candidate identifications, improving isomer discrimination and overall identification confidence.
impact: Demonstrates a practical application of conditional transformers for domain-adaptive spectrum prediction and downstream rescoring, offering a template for ML-driven improvements in proteomics workflows and instrument-agnostic spectral models.
visual_elements: Schematic of the transformer model with an 'energy' conditioning input (slider icon) feeding into the encoder/decoder.
Overlay plots of predicted vs observed spectra at low/medium/high collision energies showing improved fragment coverage.
Bar or violin chart comparing identification confidence / isomer discrimination before and after rescoring.
Pipeline flowchart: raw spectra → SpecGP prediction (energy-conditioned) → rescoring → improved identifications.
paper_title: SpecGP as a transformer-based model for predicting energy-adaptable structural spectra of glycopeptides
paper_authors: Xianyong Wang, Rui Song, Zhuangzhuang Feng, Shisheng Sun
